newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil strong as U.S., Italy buy again.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil strong as U.S., Italy buy again.

text.p: Fuel oil rose sharply in Europe as more product was sucked into the U.S. and Italy, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded up to $115 fob ARA but bids then moved to that level, chasing offers of $117.

High sulphur cargoes were strong. A Scandinavian player sold a cargo for early December to a trader at $112.50 fob NWE. The cargo was expected to move transatlantic. This compares with Tuesday's sale of Coryton barrels at $114.50 cif.
While some were surprised at that strength, another refiner heard a bid, from the buyer of the Scandinavian barrels, at $110 fob Lavera for high density, high sulphur barrels.
Italian demand for low sulphur has been strong too.

A Rotterdam refiner was heard selling 50,000 tonnes at around $10 over the quoted fob NWE high, delivered to Italy. Another trader was heard selling a cargo at a floating price, while a third trader was heard having sold some 100,000 tonnes over a couple of months, on a crude-related basis.
A Spanish low sulphur straight-run cargo was also heard sold into Italy at $10 over the quoted high cif.
